==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|mēt|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/miːt/}} ** {{audio|en|en-uk-to meet.ogg|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/mit/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-meet.ogg|a=GA}} * {{rhymes|en|iːt|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|meat|mete}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*meh₂d- (meet)}} From {{inh|en|enm|meten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mētan||to meet, find, encounter}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*mōtijan||to meet}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mōtijaną||to meet}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*meh₂d-|id=meet|t=to come, meet}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|met}}, {{m|sco|mete}}, {{m|sco|meit||to meet}}, {{cog|frr|meet}}, {{m|frr|mätje}}, {{m|frr|möt|t=to meet}}, {{cog|fy|mette}}, {{m|fy|moetsje|t=to meet}}, {{cog|nl|ontmoeten|t=to meet}}, {{cog|nds|möten|t=to meet}}, {{cog|da|møde|t=to meet}}, {{cog|ovd|my̨öt|t=to meet}}, {{cog|fo|møta|t=to meet}}, {{cog|is|mæta|t=to meet}}, {{cog|nb|møte|t=to meet}}, {{cog|nn|møta}}, {{m|nn|møte|t=to meet}}, {{cog|sv|möta|t=to meet}}. Related to {{l|en|moot}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|met}} # To make contact (with someone) while in proximity. ## {{senseid|en|encounter by accident}}To come face to face with by [[accident]]; to [[encounter]]. ##: {{ux|en|Fancy '''meeting''' you here! Guess who I '''met''' at the supermarket today?}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1899|author=w:Hughes Mearns|title={{w|Antigonish (poem)|Antigonish}} |passage=Yesterday, upon the stair
I '''met''' a man who wasn’t there
He wasn’t there again today
I wish, I wish he’d go away{{nb...}}}} ## To come face to face with someone by arrangement. ##: {{ux|en|Let's '''meet''' at the station at 9 o'clock.}} ##* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=10|passage=With a little manœuvring they contrived to '''meet''' on the doorstep which was {{...}} in a boiling stream of passers-by, hurrying business people speeding past in a flurry of fumes and dust in the bright haze.}} ## To get [[acquaint]]ed with someone. ##: {{ux|en|I'm pleased to '''meet''' you! I'd like you to '''meet''' a colleague of mine.}} ##: {{ux|en|I '''met''' my husband through a mutual friend at a party. It wasn't love at first sight; in fact, we couldn't stand each other at first!}} ##: {{ux|en|José, I don't think you've '''met''' my friend Maria.}} ##* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I |passage=Captain Edward Carlisle{{...}}felt a curious sensation of helplessness seize upon him as he met her steady gaze,{{nb...}}; he could not tell what this prisoner might do. He cursed the fate which had assigned such a duty, cursed especially that fate which forced a gallant soldier to '''meet''' so superb a woman as this under handicap so hard.}} # {{lb|en|of groups}} To come together. ## To [[gather]] for a formal or social discussion; to hold a [[meeting]]. ##: {{ux|en|I '''met''' with them several times. The government ministers '''met''' today to start the negotiations.}} ##* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|III |passage=At half-past nine on this Saturday evening, the parlour of the Salutation Inn, High Holborn, contained most of its customary visitors.{{...}}In former days every tavern of repute kept such a room for its own select circle, a club, or society, of habitués, who '''met''' every evening, for a pipe and a cheerful glass.}} ## To come together in [[conflict]]. ##* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|12.55|2|X|lv|passage=Sir said Epynegrys is þt the rule of yow [[errant|arraunt]] [[knights|knyghtes]] for to make a [[knight|knyght]] to Iuste will he or [[nill|nyll]]
As for that [[said|sayd]] Dynadan make the [[ready|redy]]
for here is for me
And there with [[all|al]] they [[spurred|spored]] [[their|theyr]] horses & '''mett''' to gyders [[so]]o hard that Epynegrys smote [[down|doune]] sir Dynadan}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=6|passage=Weapons more violent, when next we '''meet''',
May serve to better us and worse our foes.|year=1873}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-07|author=w:Gary Younge| volume=188| issue=26| page=18| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/jun/02/hypocrisy-lies-at-heart-bradley-manning-trial Hypocrisy lies at heart of Manning prosecution]| passage=The dispatches{{...}} also exposed the blatant discrepancy between the west's professed values and actual foreign policies. Having lectured the Arab world about democracy for years, its collusion in suppressing freedom was undeniable as protesters were '''met''' by weaponry and tear gas made in the west, employed by a military trained by westerners.}} ## {{lb|en|sports}} To [[play]] a match. ##: {{ux|en|England and Holland will '''meet''' in the final.}} # To make physical or perceptual contact. ## To [[converge]] and finally [[touch]] or [[intersect]]. ##: {{ux|en|The two streets '''meet''' at a crossroad half a mile away.}} ##* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I|passage=Captain Edward Carlisle, soldier as he was, martinet as he was, felt a curious sensation of helplessness seize upon him as he '''met''' her steady gaze, her alluring smile; he could not tell what this prisoner might do}} ## To [[touch]] or [[hit]] (something) while [[move|moving]]. ##: {{ux|en|The right wing of the car '''met''' the column in the garage, leaving a dent.}} ## To [[adjoin]], be physically [[touching]]. ##: {{ux|en|The carpet '''meets''' the wall at this side of the room. The forest '''meets''' the sea along this part of the coast.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[counter]] [[equally]]; to [[match]]. ### To respond to (an argument etc.) with something equally convincing; to [[refute]]. ###* {{RQ:Bramah Max Carrados Mysteries|passage=Carrados knew quite enough of flint implements—as indeed he seemed to know enough of any subject beneath the sun—to be able to talk on level terms with an expert, and he was quite equal to '''meeting''' a reference to Evans or to Nadaillac with another.}} ###: {{ux|en|He '''met''' every objection to the trip with another reason I should go.}} # To [[satisfy]]; to [[comply]] with. #: {{ux|en|This proposal '''meets''' my requirements. The company agrees to '''meet''' the cost of any repairs.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=70| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579879-buy-out-firm-really-does-focus-operational-improvements-engineers Engineers of a different kind]| passage=Private-equity nabobs bristle at being dubbed mere financiers.{{...}}Much of their pleading is public-relations bluster. Clever financial ploys are what have made billionaires of the industry’s veterans. “Operational improvement” in a portfolio company has often meant little more than promising colossal bonuses to sitting chief executives if they '''meet''' ambitious growth targets. That model is still prevalent today.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To balance or come out correct. # To perceive; to come to a knowledge of; to have personal acquaintance with; to experience; to suffer. #: {{ux|en|The eye '''met''' a horrid sight. He '''met''' his fate.}} #* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Man|passage=Of vice or virtue, whether blest or curst,
Which '''meets''' contempt, or which compassion first.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XXIII|40|{{...}} And all we '''met''' was fair and good,
⁠And all was good that Time could bring, {{...}}}} # To be [[mix]]ed with, to be [[combine]]d with [[aspect]]s of. #* {{RQ:Fry Liar|page=19|passage=‘I’m planning a sort of ''[[fabliau]]'' comparing this place with a [[fascist]] state,’ said Sampson, ‘sort of ''{{w|Animal Farm}}'' '''meets''' ''{{w|Arturo Ui}}'' . . .’}} =====Usage notes===== In the sense "come face to face with someone by arrangement", ''meet'' is sometimes used with the preposition ''with''. Nonetheless, some state that as a transitive verb in the context "to come together by chance or arrangement", ''meet'' (as in ''meet (someone)'') does not require a preposition between verb and object; the phrase ''meet with (someone)'' is deemed incorrect.
